title: Aromatic Charred Norwegian Boudin Noir Tagine
description: A hearty Norwegian dish featuring charred boudin noir, flambe, and aromatic spices, cooked in a traditional clay tagine, perfect for a cozy dinner, and FODMAP friendly.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
Season the boudin noir links with cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper.
Heat the olive oil in the clay tagine over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion to the tagine and cook until caramelized, stirring occasionally.
Add the grated ginger and garlic infused oil to the tagine and cook for 1 minute.
Add the seasoned boudin noir links to the tagine and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the chicken broth to the tagine and bring to a simmer.
Cover the tagine with a lid and transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 20 minutes, then remove the lid and continue baking for an additional 10 minutes, or until the boudin noir is charred and crispy.
Remove the tagine from the oven and carefully flambe the dish with the flambe liquor.
Serve the charred boudin noir hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
